requirement: Habeas MUST bundle a `habeas-requirements` skill whose description tells agents to use it during design sessions and before changing code, tests, or requirement text in a Habeas project, including when the user asks for a feature, bug fix, or other change without mentioning requirements.
rationale:
The requirement `requirements.cli.requirements_skill` has three obligations: (1) a `habeas-requirements` skill is bundled; (2) its description tells agents to use it during design sessions and before changing code, tests, or requirement text in a Habeas project; (3) that includes cases where the user asks for a feature, bug fix, or other change without mentioning requirements.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_requirements_skill_is_used_for_design_and_before_any_change]` covers all three. It calls the helper `description("habeas-requirements")`. That helper uses `skill_md` and `skill_files`, which `include_str!` `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md`, and it extracts the front-matter `description:` line. It panics if the skill is unknown or has no description. So the test fails if the bundled skill is missing, if the skill is not registered under that name, or if the description is absent.

The test then asserts that the description contains three phrases:
- "Use during design sessions and before changing code, tests, or requirement text in a project that tracks requirements with Habeas" covers obligation 2.
- "even when the user only asks for a feature, bug fix," covers the feature and bug-fix part of obligation 3.
- "and never says \"requirement\"" covers the part of obligation 3 about the user not mentioning requirements.

The actual `SKILL.md` description contains all of these phrases, so the assertions match the requirement's wording. A description that dropped the design-session trigger, the pre-change trigger, or the "without mentioning requirements" clause would fail.

The phrase-based assertions are brittle but not too weak. I found no plausible violating description that the test would accept. The `src` search found no source code that embeds the skills, so I could not check how bundling works beyond the skill file existing in the assets and being included by the test. I did not treat that as a gap, because the requirement's content obligation concerns the description text.

text: Habeas MUST bundle a `habeas-requirements` skill whose description tells agents to use it during design sessions and before changing code, tests, or requirement text in a Habeas project, including when the user asks for a feature, bug fix, or other change without mentioning requirements.
